results.summary_before: This design counts the number of digital pulses occurring within a time interval across four input channels. The counts are periodically output using a serial output. It is intended for low-power wake-up sensor interfaces, acoustic event detection, non-destructive testing, and particle counting. The design is a generic pulse-counting digital building block.
results.summary: This design is a variable duty-cycle true random number generator based on seven 7-stage ring oscillators. The oscillators are enabled by an 'ena' signal and their outputs are combined at a common node. An inverter-bias system using a vDAC selects a voltage from the first four input pins. The resulting signal passes through two D flip-flops and an AND gate to produce the final random output.

results.summary_before: Convertidor de Tiempo a Digital (TDC) is a time-to-digital converter that measures the width of an input pulse and transmits the digital value via RS232. The design is intended for interfacing with time-output sensors and was tested in simulation and on an FPGA development board.

results.summary_before: This project implements a 16-bit noise-shaping delta-sigma DAC that outputs a single-bit digital signal via pulse-width modulation. The design uses a delta-sigma modulator to shape quantization noise and a PWM stage to generate the analog output. It is intended for audio applications and can be interfaced with external analog filters. The project is notable for its high-resolution digital-to-analog conversion using a simple one-bit output.
